subject: Multi-year prepay: split-pay proposal, escrow terms, and SLA credits
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@veridian.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@veridian.com
Date: 2026-11-12 09:14 PST
Subject: Budgetary ask - FY27 prepay options and split-pay scenarios

Olga,

Thanks for taking this call earlier. We need a budgetary quote for FY27 planning that covers a potential 3-year commitment (FY27–FY29). High level: 300M token-equivalent credits over three years (we expect ramping consumption). Procurement specifically wants: a) options for multi-year prepay with tiered term discounts, b) split-pay (staggered invoicing across quarters / years), c) escrow or refundable component for unused credits, and d) how SLA credits would be applied if monthly SLOs are missed.

Can you send a pro forma that shows 1) annual prepay (no term discount), 2) a 3-year prepay with a term discount and proposed ramp schedule, and 3) a split-pay scenario we can align to FY budgets (they prefer not to fund a single lump sum). Also include invoicing instructions and PO requirements — Veridian requires the expected invoice schedule to map to their finance cycles.

We have a hard internal deadline of 11/30 to get something into procurement for FY27 commit.

Best,
Maya
Maya Singh
Head of AI Partnerships | Veridian Financial
From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@veridian.com>
Cc: procurement@veridian.com, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12 13:02 PST
Subject: RE: Budgetary ask - FY27 prepay options and split-pay scenarios

Hi Maya — appreciate the clarity and deadline. Attached is a concise pro forma (Proforma_Invoice_Verdian_MultiYear_2027-29.pdf) and a draft SOW for your legal team. Summary of the options (high level):

1) Annual prepay (baseline)
- 100% invoiced upfront each fiscal year
- No multi-year term discount
- Standard Net30 invoicing

2) 3-year prepay (recommended for unit economics)
- Proposed term discount: 20% on list unit price across the committed term
- Proposed ramp schedule (consumption allocation): Year 1 = 40% of total committed credits, Year 2 = 35%, Year 3 = 25%
- Billing options: a) Single upfront invoice for full term (eligible for full term discount), or b) Split-pay: 50% Year1 at signing, 25% at start of Year2, 25% at start of Year3 (this keeps discounts while aligning to budgets)
- Carry-forward: up to 10% of annual committed units can carry to the following year (one-time carry-forward; expires at term end)

3) Split-pay / escrow variant (for capital planning)
- We can place the Year1 portion in a restricted escrow account (third-party custodian) with defined release triggers tied to usage milestones or time (escrowed funds refundable pro rata for unused credits at term end)
- Escrow amount is configurable; suggested default = 30% of Year1 invoice for customers requesting refundability

SLA credits & governance
- SLA: 99.9% monthly availability target by default
- SLA credits: modeled as a % credit applied to the following invoice if we miss monthly SLOs (capped at 50% of that month’s invoice under the standard draft). We can adjust cap by negotiation — please indicate target cap.

Next steps: attached proforma shows line-item pricing for each option and a sample split-pay schedule mapped to fiscal quarters. If you prefer, I can provision an updated proforma with a Net45 payment term (we can also discuss escrow percentage and SLA credit cap).

Attachments: Proforma_Invoice_Verdian_MultiYear_2027-29.pdf, SOW_Redwood_Veridian_Draft.docx

Thanks — I’ll be available to jump on a quick call to walk procurement through the invoicing schedule.

Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13 10:17 PST
Subject: Internal: Veridian - discount / finance levers

Quick internal note before you reply to Veridian:
- Finance reviewed the proforma. They are willing to move the term discount to 22% (from 20%) to help close, conditional on: Net45 terms and a split-pay schedule (not full upfront) so their cash exposure is limited.
- Escrow: recommend limiting escrow to 25% of Year1 rather than 30% to reduce administrative friction. Escrow should be refundable pro rata at term end for unused credits.
- SLA credit cap: finance/legal prefer a 25% monthly cap (not 50%) to limit liability. We can offer a 25% cap with a 50% cap on a case-by-case basis tied to committed spend.
- Commercial sweetener: offer a one-time implementation credit ($50,000) applied in Q1 if they sign the 3-year prepay and provide PO by 11/30.

If you want me to escalate to Revenue Ops or Legal for special Net60/other terms, let me know.

-Marcus
VP, Sales Operations
From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@veridian.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@veridian.com
Date: 2026-11-14 08:46 PST
Subject: RE: Budgetary ask - updated pro forma and split-pay structure

Maya — attached is an updated pro forma (attachment) reflecting the agreed commercial levers we can extend if Veridian signs by 11/30:

Highlights (updated):
- 3-year prepay: 22% term discount applied to list unit price
- Ramp schedule: Year1 = 40% / Year2 = 35% / Year3 = 25%
- Split-pay schedule: 50% invoiced at signing (applies to Year1/partial Year2), then 25% at start of Year2, 25% at start of Year3
- Escrow: limited to 25% of Year1 invoice, held in a restricted escrow account and refundable pro rata for unused credits at term end
- SLA credits: capped at 25% of the affected month’s invoice; we will auto-apply credits to the next invoice.
- Payment terms: Net45 for multi-year prepay (finance-approved)
- One-time implementation credit: $50,000 applied in Q1 following contract execution if PO is received by 11/30

Please review the attached pro forma and draft SOW; I included an explicit invoicing schedule to map to procurement’s fiscal calendar. If these look good, I can push the agreement to DocuSign and share the link.

Note: procurement asked about data residency language in the SOW — we flagged the section for legal review. If Veridian needs EU data residency clauses we can add an addendum (will require Legal sign-off).

Olga
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Olga — thanks for the quick turnaround. Veridian is generally aligned to the updated commercial terms. We will: 1) issue a PO for the indicated split-pay 3-year prepay (PO attached as PO_VRDN_2026_1115.pdf), 2) accept Net45, and 3) request the escrow be implemented per the attached SOW.

Two small asks before we sign:
- Legal needs an explicit EU data residency addendum included in the SOW (we will provide redline language this week)
- Can the SLA credit cap be bumped to 35% instead of 25%? We are willing to accept an escrow and Net45 in exchange for an elevated cap to 35%.

If you can send a DocuSign packet with the PO referenced and updated cap option (marked as alternative commercial term), we will push the PO through approvals today.

Thanks — Amir
Sr. Procurement Manager | Veridian Financial
